t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup. Background split on a diagonal from deep navy on the left to limestone on the right. A giant outline display word is cropped off the top edge and repeated in layered outlines at lower left as a motion echo; a huge solid italic word is cropped at the bottom right. Headline top left with one phrase in steel blue. Four square-cornered cards rise left to right as a staircase, each with a mono step number and chevron arrow above and labelled fields for <CONTENT>. Thin elbow connector lines with arrowheads.
signature_idea: Huge cropped START and GO words frame a staircase of situation cards, so the router literally reads as a start-to-go climb.
strengths: the staircase makes the four entry points feel like progression
card fields (situation, send, back) are a clear router pattern
strong visual memory for a services page
weaknesses: bold heavy headline and italic display words are loud, off-brand vs calm Geist light
outline type behind cards hurts legibility
invented hype subhead ('We bridge the gap') breaks voice
overlapping cards and stray duplicate numbers create clutter
staircase implies a sequence where the situations are actually alternatives
brand_fit_why: Uses navy/limestone and a steel-blue accent, but the heavy italic kinetic type and busy layering contradict the calm, precise, light-headline brand.
